surprises.description: Landstar’s revenue was modestly above the preview’s $1.49 billion benchmark: overall revenue grew 25% year over year, and truck revenue of $1.407 billion exceeded the $1.36 billion estimate. Truck growth was also stronger than the preview’s segment estimate, driven by 25% higher revenue per load and 3% more loads.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Overall revenue rose 25% year-over-year in Q3 2026, with truck revenue up 29% to $1.407 billion driven by a 25% increase in truck revenue per load and 3% more truck loads hauled.”

surprises.description: Insurance and claims were substantially worse than the preview’s base case, with $55.3 million of costs and about $22 million of unfavorable prior-year adjustments. The preview’s base case assumed $40 million of claims and no new reserve charge; even its bear case assumed a smaller $10–12 million additional adverse development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Insurance and claims costs surged to $55.3 million from $33 million a year earlier, including ~$22 million of net unfavorable prior-year claim adjustments ($0.47 per share), comprising $13 million in adverse actuarial reserve adjustments and $8 million from two claim settlements.” Management “withdrew formal insurance guidance” and described a quarterly run rate between $35 million and $55 million, with a trailing four-quarter average near $46 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base” scenario: “Insurance/claims $40M” and “claims elevated but stable; no new reserve charge.” “Bear” scenario: “another ~$10–12M adverse development.”

surprises.description: BCO truck additions substantially exceeded the preview’s already-positive reference point: net additions were 165 for the quarter, versus 68 in Q2, and the count increased further in the first four weeks of Q4. The preview said a bull case needed net adds to accelerate past 68.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net BCO truck count increased by 165 during the quarter, the strongest quarterly improvement since Q3 2021, and rose a further 22% in the first four weeks of Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “BCO net adds accelerate past +68” was listed as an operational requirement for the bull scenario; the preview also called +68 “the best in four years.”

surprises.description: October truck demand and pricing remained stronger than the preview’s cautious seasonal setup suggested: loads were about 7% above October 2025 and revenue per load about 29% higher, with both slightly outperforming normal seasonality. The preview flagged the possibility that pricing had peaked after July and noted early-October spot-rate softness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “October truck loads were approximately 7% above October 2025 and revenue per load was approximately 29% above October 2025, both slightly outperforming normal seasonality.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether July’s “+26%” revenue-per-load growth was “the peak or the run rate,” and noted that “DAT spot rates dipped 2–3 cents/mile in early October as load posts cooled.”

surprises.description: Landstar returned more capital through buybacks than the preview’s latest reported pace suggested: buybacks reached about $65 million through 39 weeks, versus $24.1 million reported through Q2. This is a concrete step-up from the pace the preview highlighted as potentially increasing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company returned ~$175 million to shareholders through the first 39 weeks (~$110 million dividends, ~$65 million buybacks) and declared a regular $0.44 quarterly dividend.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “YTD buybacks were only $24.1M against $280.9M net cash”; the preview said “a repurchase step-up would read as management calling the de-rating overdone.”

surprises.description: Management put a specific potential revenue benefit on the preview’s broader idea that post-Montgomery pressures could help Landstar gain business: higher insurance renewals for smaller brokers and owner-operators could make Landstar a “safe haven,” with roughly $100 million of potential new agent revenue. The preview discussed a possible consolidation benefit but did not quantify this opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects the Montgomery decision to drive insurance renewals “materially higher over the next one to two years for smaller brokers and owner-operators,” positioning Landstar to capture agents and BCOs seeking a scaled “safe haven,” with “potential for roughly $100 million in new agent revenue tailwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The bull argument is that Montgomery is a consolidation catalyst that accrues to Landstar.”
